clarified_messages.content: Hi Dr. Kim, I'm finally here at the front.
Great, I'll meet you outside the office in five minutes. Have you brought the forms they gave you downstairs?
Yes, I have them right here. There was a nurse who asked about my allergies. Should I mention them now or later?
Mention them now—I need to add them to your chart before we move on.
Okay, the only one is penicillin. They put a sticker on the folder for it.
Alright. Do you still have the test results from last week?
Yes, they're in this envelope. Should I hand them to you now or after we're inside?
You can hand them to me here, but I'll double-check with the coordinator when we get to the desk.
Sounds good. I think she's already in—the person with the blue badge?
Right, that's Michelle. She'll help us prep everything for the procedure.
Thanks. By the way, my daughter is parked out front. Will she be able to wait in the lounge?
Yes, visitors can use the lounge on the second floor. The volunteer in the red vest will show her.
Perfect. Should I go straight to that desk now?
Yes, please. You'll need to check in with Michelle and hand her all your documents.
Alright, heading over. There's another person at the desk—is she helping too?
That's Janet, our surgical assistant. She'll verify your insurance information.
Got it. Should I give her my insurance card or just the ID?
Both, please. Janet will scan them for our records.
Handing them over now. Do you need me to sign anything today?
Yes, after you finish with Michelle and Janet, I'll need you to sign the consent forms with me in the office.
Is it okay to bring my daughter in for the signatures?
Of course. She's listed as your emergency contact, right?
Yes, that's her—Emily Brooks. Do you need her ID or just her signature?
Just her signature is fine. We'll add her phone number to your chart for the day of surgery.
Alright. Is there anything else I need to do before tomorrow morning?
Yes, you must fast after midnight and stop your medication starting tonight. Did you bring the list of meds?
Right, I have that list here in my bag. Should I hand it to you?
Yes, I'll review it now and confirm which ones need to be suspended.
Handing you the list. I stopped aspirin last week as you said.
Perfect. Do you remember the time for your check-in tomorrow?
Is it 6:30 AM at this building?
Yes, the surgical entrance here. You'll see the security guard in blue.
Will Michelle be here at that hour or someone else?
Tomorrow, it'll be Alex at the desk. He'll check you in and take you to pre-op.
Okay, I'll look for him. After surgery, where will I recover—here or elsewhere?
You'll move to the recovery unit on the third floor, just across from the elevators.
Is my daughter allowed up there?
Yes, visiting hours start at 7 AM for family.
Great. Will someone tell her when I'm out of surgery?
Yes, the volunteer in the recovery lounge will notify Emily as soon as you're settled.
Thank you. Will I get physical therapy right away?
The therapist will visit you there tomorrow afternoon.
Is it the same person as last week?
No, tomorrow it'll be John, not Lisa.
Should I call anyone if I have questions tonight?
You can reach my office number, or after hours call the on-call nurse. Her info is in your packet.
Okay, I see a number here but it's not labeled. Is it hers?
If it's ending in -2384, that's the nurse's cell.
That's it. To confirm, I fast tonight, arrive here by 6:30 AM, bring my ID and insurance, and check in with Alex at the desk?
That's exactly right. I'll meet you outside pre-op once you're checked in.
Thank you, Dr. Kim. Is there anything else you need from me now?
Just a signature on those forms. Let's go to my office now.
Heading there. See you inside.
I'll be there in two minutes.
It's nice that the weather's so mild today. Makes it easier to get here.
Definitely. Last week was freezing; glad it's better today.
Will I need a walker after surgery or just crutches?
Just crutches for the first week. The therapist will show you how to use them.
Do you have any paperwork about the exercises I need to do?
Yes, I'll include a physical therapy pamphlet in your packet today.
Alright, thank you. See you in the office.
